SITS RECEIVING — complete flow (read-only from IFS · Ownership from PO prefix · status-driven: To-be-counted -> count, Inspected -> tag · device registration · re-tag / cancel-tags / audit)

SETUP · Admin — Device Registration: register every device (4-port readers, gate readers, ZT411 printer, laser engraver, weigh/reel machines, handhelds) to its STORE / DEPARTMENT. A user may only use devices registered to their store.
IFS · Store operator: creates the Gate Entry in IFS when the goods physically arrive (this is what SITS then polls).
SITS reads (SELECT): GATE_ENTRY_HEADER (key = gate_entry_no).
SITS (read-only DB link): every 5 minutes — and on Refresh — SELECT GATE_ENTRY_HEADER to find new / updated gate entries.

New gate entry
not seen before?
SITS reads (SELECT): the gate-entry lines + item master (INVENTORY_PART) + Part Catalogue serialized flag (SERIAL_TRACKING_CODE) + COC / test-report references.
SITS: for the new gate entry, SELECT only the required line fields (part_no, challan_qty, status, hold, charges_approved, conversion_factor, inventory_qty, note_text, disposition).
SITS DB: cached gate-entry line details.
SITS: derive Ownership from the gate-entry PO prefix (REP PO / REP FOC = repair; PO = company) using HAL's rule. Read-only — nothing written to IFS.
IFS · QC: inspects the goods and sets the line status → Inspected / Hold / Rejected.

Line STATUS?
To-be-counted → count
Inspected → tag
Hold → re-query
Rejected → stop
STATUS = Rejected → save as rejected in SITS and never query this line again.
If the RR line is cancelled / amended in IFS after tagging → SITS cancels (voids) those tags and keeps the audit trail.

OP: count the goods (STATUS = To-be-counted). Method Manual / Weight / Reel — item default shown, can override. Serialized = 1 item/package (1 RFID per serial). Non-serialized = enter PACKAGE DEFINITION (qty per package). Optional 2nd-person count: per-item default (shown when receiving that item again), changeable for this gate entry.
Device — Weigh / Reel counting machine (must be registered to the operator's store; if more than one, the operator picks). Computes the counted quantity from the baseline value and returns it.
SITS: validate the counted quantity against the IFS expected quantity (INVENTORY_QTY = CHALLAN_QTY × CONVERSION_FACTOR; a blank factor = 1).
SITS DB: transit baseline count.

Counted qty =
expected qty?
No → save the count and the variance, alert the operator / managers, allow a re-count or edit (only in this first transit count).
SITS: after the count, keep re-polling this line every 5 min until STATUS = Inspected → start tagging; Hold → keep polling; Rejected → stop.

OP (STATUS = Inspected): 1) pick tag type — Label-RFID / Hard-RFID / Barcode-only; 2) (optional) colour pattern & code — operator selects by material type / form; 3) (optional) top-marking — 1 photo compulsory + up to 2 more (max 3); text boxes = number of photos (max 3).
Device — handheld camera: on a request from SITS captures the top-marking photo(s) and returns them.
SITS: 1) substitute (Y ≠ X) — take Y from the RR reference, keep the X↔Y link (approval optional); 2) convert the quantity to HAL's stocking unit (item master INVENTORY_PART, key CONTRACT + PART_NO).

Serialized item?
(PART_CATALOG.SERIAL_
TRACKING_CODE =
'Serial Tracking')

Serialized: read serials from GATE_ENTRY_DETAIL.NOTE_TEXT (comma-separated; max 50 per serial, 2000 total) → 1 tag per serial. If serials missing in IFS → BLOCK tagging + email alert to BOTH the store person (gate-entry creator) and the QC / inspector.
SITS: for one serial at a time — generate the RFID (EPC) + barcode / QR, build the print file, and display that serial number on screen.
Device — tag printer (ZT411): prints Label-RFID and Hard-RFID tags; verify by read-back; on failure void & reprint.
Device — laser engraver: marks the barcode / QR on the raw-material component (rod / sheet) — NOT on the tag.
OP: stick the printed tag on the item matching the serial shown on screen; commission by read-back.
SITS: save the RFID ↔ serial link (kept only in SITS).
SITS DB: tag records (EPC↔part/serial), event log, photos.

More serials
for this line?

Non-serialized: for each package (from the package definition) generate the RFID (EPC) + barcode / QR, print & commission a tag carrying the same item and the package quantity, save; repeat per package.
SITS: link the COC / test-report (via FTP to the HAL scan server) — fetch & show on read, no permanent copy stored.
OP: bring all goods going to one destination to the 4-port reader and touch 'Start' to begin the transfer session.
Reader (4-port): read the first RFID tag and send its tag ID to the server.
SITS reads: charge-approval per line — CHARGES_APPROVED = True / False.
Server (SITS): find that tag's gate entry, then return the whole gate's list of tag IDs — each with its charge-approval status — to the reader.
Reader: for each scanned tag, check it against the list — approved → show the item; not approved → BLOCKING ERROR (a new tag not in the list makes the reader re-request).
OP: click 'Stop', then select the destination holding store.
SITS: create a Transfer ID for the charge-approved tags only (may span gate entries); store the tag↔Transfer-ID map in Redis; set each tag's status to 'Sent to Holding'.
SITS DB / Redis: open Transfer ID + its tag list.
OP: take the goods out of the Transit store through the exit gate.
Device — fixed gate (anti-theft) readers: continuously read the departing tags.

Tag has a valid
Transfer ID?
(barcode-only heavy
goods are exempt)
No → raise an anti-theft ALARM (in-app + Security) and stop the item from leaving.
Reader (4-port at holding): send the Transfer ID to the server.
Server (SITS): return all the tag IDs that belong to this Transfer ID to the reader.
Reader: as the OP scans the arriving tags, audit each against the Transfer ID's list and check all are present.
SITS: produce the receipt audit report — FOUND / NOT-FOUND / EXTRA. Missing → alert managers; found → status 'Received at Holding'.
EXTRA package (a tag not in this Transfer ID) → alert Transit; the item is returned to the Transit store; Transit picks the correct destination and a NEW Transfer ID is generated.
SITS: reconcile any substitute (keep the X↔Y link).
OP (serialized): scan the RFID; if the tag's serial ≠ the serial on screen, update the correct serial (repeat until it matches), then continue.
OP: re-count the goods at holding (same method as the transit count).
Device — Weigh / Reel counting machine (registered to the store): returns the re-counted quantity.

Holding count =
number of RFID
tags received?
No → flag the discrepancy and proceed (no edit at holding); alert the managers.
IFS · Store operator: receives the goods and assigns the bin / location in IFS.
SITS reads: LOCATION_NO / position from the location master (BIN / ROW / TIER are blank; the location is the composite LOCATION_NO).
SITS: map the assigned LOCATION_NO (bin / position) to each RFID — only the bin / location carries a tag; position is logical.
OP: put-away with the handheld at ~10 cm — Find the location tag, then Place the packet (scan bin + packet) to confirm the correct location.
Device — handheld: works offline, syncs when docked in the LAN cradle; alerts if left undocked too long.
Wrong location → the handheld beeps and asks the operator to re-scan the correct one.
Tag damaged / unreadable / lost → void the old EPC (keep the audit trail), reprint & re-commission a new tag, then continue.
SITS: when the handheld re-docks, sync the placement and save the storage confirmation.
SITS DB: storage confirmation.
Physical-stock verification (periodic): a handheld walk-through reads the location tag and the nearby tags, maps them to LOCATION_NO, and reports FOUND / NOT-FOUND / EXTRA against IFS stock.
